sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial and industrial centre of Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. The upper left is taken by Dover Pond and the Rockaway River, which bends down the sheet toward the right. On the pond shore stand the buildings of the Ulster Iron Works: a large rolling mill with its furnaces and boilers, a machine shop and storage building, a 16 inch mill, iron ware houses, a pig iron shed and a shipping house, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks running past them. The bed of the old Morris Canal is marked as filled in across the middle of the sheet. Below it the main business blocks of Dover line West Blackwell Street, North Warren Street and South Warren Street, with North Sussex Street and South Sussex Street along the east edge. They include the Baker Theatre, a presbyterian church in a walled lot, the Dover Trust Company and National Union Bank, a large department store, the Masonic Hall, Elite Hall, the Hotel Dover and the Post Office. A municipal building with police and fire headquarters stands at the upper right, beside a Free Methodist church and an I.O.O.F. hall on West Clinton Street. At the lower left Prospect Street runs diagonally past a B.P.O.E. lodge and a Royal Arcanum hall, with a garage and the telephone exchange nearby. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the foot of the sheet. Water pipes with their sizes are lettered in most streets, and street widths are given.
notes: Canal is the street along the foot of the iron works block; spacing from West Blackwell Street matches Bassett Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Pequannock (north) and North Warren (south) are one street; OpenStreetMap changes the name at Bassett Highway.
West Dickerson Street is cut by the sheet edge, so its junction with South Warren Street was placed by hand (medium confidence).
50 ft. Downtown Dover: W. Blackwell, Warren, Sussex, Canal (now Bassett Highway), Dickerson; Ulster Iron Works, Dover Pond. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the blocks of central Dover east of Sussex Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. It runs from East Clinton Street across the top, through Richards Avenue and the Rockaway River, to East Blackwell Street and East Dickerson Street, with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks and the passenger station along the bottom edge. North Sussex Street and South Sussex Street bound the left side and North Bergen Street and South Bergen Street the right, with North and South Morris Street and North and South Essex Street between. The upper left blocks hold small shops, Cottage Row and Schwarz Place, with the old canal bed marked as filled in across a wedge-shaped block, a laundry, a printing works and a wagon shed. The Rockaway River and the Central Railroad of New Jersey cross the sheet diagonally; on the river bank stand a beer bottler, a plumber and a concrete floor works. The Birch and Bassett garage and auto repair shop stands in the middle of the sheet, and east of North Essex Street the Sacred Heart parochial school, convent and church and a row of dwellings face River Street. South of the river are a church, the Bergen Building, the National Biscuit Company warehouse, a movie house, a business college, the Salvation Army, a hotel and a large garage, with the Mansion House and the Lackawanna House at lower left. St. John's Episcopal Church, its club and a parsonage stand at the lower right. Water pipe sizes and street widths are lettered.
notes: Canal Street at the west edge continues the street called Canal on sheet 2, which matches Bassett Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Foundry Street, Cottage Row and Schwarz Place are not named streets in OpenStreetMap.
The old canal bed is marked as filled in.
50 ft. East of Sussex to Bergen, Clinton to Dickerson; downtown business blocks. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the eastern part of central Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Richards Avenue runs along the top edge. Below it lie four blocks of dwellings between North Bergen Street, Hudson Street, Passaic Street and Union Street, with River Street along their lower side, a church mission and the Bethlehem Congregational Church among them. The Rockaway River runs across the middle of the sheet in a straight channel with the Central Railroad of New Jersey on its north bank, and the lumber yard and coal pockets of the Dover Lumber Company stand beside it. South of the river, East Blackwell Street is lined with a continuous row of shops, a garage with room for twenty five cars, bowling alleys, a printing works, a hardware and drug store, a wagon shed and the Swedish Evangelical Lutheran Church, with Mercer Street at the right edge. South of East Blackwell Street, between South Bergen Street and the street lettered W. V. Shoemaker, are more stores, garages and repair shops, Grant Place and the very large lumber sheds of the Dover Lumber Company and the Park Union Lumber Company. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the lower part with its tracks and yard, and below it are the Dover Boiler Works with a boiler shop, machine shop and forge shop, a signal tower and an office. South Dickerson Street and Monmouth Avenue are lettered at the foot of the sheet. Water pipe sizes and street widths are given.
notes: The street lettered W. V. Shoemaker south of East Blackwell Street lies on the line of Union Street.
Mercer Street lies at the right edge of the sheet and is only partly drawn.
50 ft. Richards Av. to the boiler works, N. Bergen to Mercer; Rockaway River, D.L.&W. station. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the northeast side of Dover along East Blackwell Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Richards Avenue runs along the top, Mercer Street along the left edge, and Brook Street meets Richards Avenue near the right. On Richards Avenue at the upper left stand the works of the McKiernan Terry Drill Company, makers of rock drills and mining machinery, with two machine shops, a pattern shop, a blacksmith shop and an office, and next to them the grain elevator, stable and wagon house of a feed company. The right half of the north block is a row of dwellings numbered 122 to 152, with the Birch and Bassett coal yard and its coal pockets behind them. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and the Rockaway River cross the sheet from lower left to upper right between the two blocks of houses. South of the river, dwellings numbered 133 to 203 face East Blackwell Street on long narrow lots running down to the river. South of East Blackwell Street are greenhouses with hot beds, a garage, a few dwellings and the Sussex Overall Company works, which make knickers and bloomers. The lower third of the sheet is the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad with a freight yard, a locomotive house and a turntable. A scale bar, a north arrow and the legend not exposed beyond fill the foot of the sheet. Water pipes with their sizes are lettered in the streets.
notes: Brook Street is the south end of Nelson Street in OpenStreetMap.
River Street is lettered at the left edge only.
50 ft. Mercer to Brook St. (now Nelson St.), Richards Av. to the freight yard and turntable. One part; control mostly along one line.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the northeast edge of Dover along East Blackwell Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Richards Avenue runs along the top, from Brook Street at the left past Lynn Street and Trenton Street to North Salem Street at the right edge; East Blackwell Street crosses the sheet below it and meets North Salem Street and South Salem Street at the right. The upper left holds a few dwellings numbered 154 to 180 on Richards Avenue. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet from left to right, and the Rockaway River divides into two channels that wind across the middle and lower parts, one passing under an iron bridge on East Blackwell Street. On the north bank stand a bottling works, with storage buildings and a well and pump, the Keystone Fuel and Supply Company coal pockets and the Crystal Ice Company ice plant with its freezing tanks and ice storage, at the right beside North Salem Street. South of Richards Avenue, between the river and East Blackwell Street, are scattered dwellings, a warehouse not in use and a filling station. South of East Blackwell Street are a garage, a garage and storage building for state highways, dwellings and a sign company with a candy store and auto sales on the corner of South Salem Street. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the lower part of the sheet. Water pipes and street widths are lettered.
notes: Brook Street is the south end of Nelson Street in OpenStreetMap.
Lynn Street and Trenton Street meet Richards Avenue at the top edge and are only partly drawn.
50 ft. Brook St. (Nelson) to Salem St., Richards Av. to the D.L.&W.; Rockaway River. One part; weak control along Richards Av.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows a residential district of northwest Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. It lies between Central Avenue along the top and West McFarlan Street and West Clinton Street across the lower right, with West Clinton Street running down the left side, Baker Street through the middle and Pequannock Street along the right edge. Fairview Avenue and Front Street cross the sheet from left to right. Nearly all the buildings are frame dwellings with outbuildings, on lots with their house numbers lettered. A blank strip at the left edge belongs to the adjoining sheet. In the lower part a bank, labelled as the top of the bank, runs across the sheet, and the Dover Water Department stands on West McFarlan Street, with a work shop and an office. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses diagonally from the lower right toward the centre left,, and carries sidings and two warehouses near the bottom. A freight house stands at the lower right corner, and the edge of Dover Pond appears at the foot of the sheet. At the lower left the diagonal West Clinton Street is lined with dwellings and a plumber's shop. Water pipes with their sizes are lettered in most streets, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are given.
notes: West Clinton Street changes direction: it runs north and south at the left of the sheet and diagonally past West McFarlan Street at the lower right.
The sheet is turned about 7.7 degrees from north according to the fit.
50 ft. North-west Dover, Central Av. to W. McFarlan, Pequannock, Baker; Dover Pond. One part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the residential and light-commercial blocks of north-central Dover between Fairview Avenue and Segur Street on the north and West and East Clinton Street on the south, from Pequannock Street on the west to Hoagland Avenue and Foundry Street on the east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page. The western blocks along Pequannock Street and North Sussex Street are lined with frame dwellings; the block between them north of West McFarlan Street holds the North Side Public School, a lodge and school annex building, and a retaining wall along Sussex Street. East of Sussex the Grace M. E. Church stands at the corner of Sanford Street and East McFarlan Street, and the blocks between Sanford, Segur and Hinchman Avenue are residential, including a building labelled The Colonnade. South of McFarlan Street the two blocks toward Clinton Street are denser and more commercial: a bakery, the Gulf Construction Company auto truck storage, the Reid Ice Cream Company ice house, J. N. Brown storage, a garage for one hundred cars, an office, the Dover Band headquarters and meeting rooms, and the Loyal Order of Moose lodge rooms with a public library on West Clinton Street. Foundry Street runs along the east side of these blocks, and beyond it the old canal basin of the Morris Canal is marked as filled in, with only a few small buildings. Water pipes with their sizes are drawn in most streets, and street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered.
notes: The old canal basin east of Foundry Street is marked as filled in.
Segur, Sanford and Foundry are lettered without a suffix; today Segur Street, Sanford Street; Foundry is not a named street in OpenStreetMap.

50 ft. Pilot. Fairview Av./Segur to W. and E. Clinton, Pequannock to Hoagland Av. and Foundry; North Side Public School, Grace M.E. Church, Moose lodge and public library; old canal basin filled in. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the residential blocks of northern Dover on both sides of East McFarlan Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Segur Street and Sanford Street cross the upper left; Hoagland Avenue, Mount Hope Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run north and south; and McDavit Place, Locust Avenue and Oak Street angle off at the upper right. Locust Hill Cemetery lies just beyond the top edge. Nearly all the buildings are frame dwellings with outbuildings. South of East McFarlan Street the old canal basin and the old canal bed, both marked as filled in, cut diagonally across the middle of the sheet, leaving large blocks of open ground. On East McFarlan Street at the right stand a garage, a milk depot, a bakery with its oven, a wagon shed and Cooks Laundry, a large works with its own sprinkler and water system. Further south are the blocks along North Essex Street, North Bergen Street, Hudson Street, Passaic Street and Union Street, between Myrtle Avenue and Richards Avenue at the foot of the sheet; they hold more dwellings and a Baptist church at the corner of Union Street and Myrtle Avenue. A pink building at the right edge belongs to the adjoining sheet. Water pipes with their sizes and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are lettered.
notes: Mount Hope Avenue north of East McFarlan Street continues south of it as North Bergen Street; OpenStreetMap carries both names at one node.
McDavit Place is Mc Davitt Place in OpenStreetMap.
The old canal basin and canal bed are marked as filled in.
50 ft. North Dover, Segur to Richards Av., Hoagland Av. to Union; Locust Hill Cemetery edge. One part.

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top, covers the northern edge of built-up Dover between Black Pond and Segur Street. Pequannock Street and North Sussex Street run north from Fairview Avenue past Central Avenue and Goodale Avenue toward Black Pond, whose shore curves across the top left corner; North Sussex Street continues north as a 45 to 66 foot road past a few scattered dwellings in blocks 440 and 2A. The blocks between Pequannock and Sussex streets (121 and 128) and those east of Sussex between Central Avenue, Losey Street and Segur Street (125, 126, 123 and 124) hold frame and a few stuccoed dwellings with sheds and auto garages; block 124 contains a small hollow-tile ice cream factory. Hinchman Avenue and Hoagland Avenue run south from Losey Street to Segur Street. The large open ground to the east, lettered Locust Hill Cemetery, is left blank apart from a drive into the cemetery off North Sussex Street. A heavy line encloses the upper right corner of the sheet, which holds a separate inset of the New Jersey Power and Light Company substation located elsewhere. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in most streets, and a hydrant stands at nearly every corner.
notes: The New Jersey Power and Light Company substation inset (part 2) is not placed: it has no street junction.

50 ft. Part 1: Goodale Av. to Segur, Pequannock to Hoagland Av., Locust Hill Cemetery, Black Pond. Part 2 (upper right, behind a heavy line): inset of the New Jersey Power and Light Co. high-tension substation, 100 ft, located about 2 miles from the post office in Rockaway Township (key map); no street junction.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: New Jersey Power & Light Co. high tension sub-station (no street junction; needs parcel corners of the substation lot or a modern outline of the substation).

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 covers the western two thirds of the page, left of the heavy vertical line that divides it from the Wharton strip. It shows a district of south-western Dover on the slope above Prospect Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Prospect Street runs diagonally across the upper left corner, and Gold Street runs east from it along the head of the map, 50 feet wide at Prospect and 55 feet wide where it meets Liberty Street. Grant Street and Liberty Street, labelled Liberty (German), run south from Gold Street between blocks 209 and 210; both are lined on the eastern side with narrow frame dwellings, with the houses numbered along the street fronts. Block 209 west of Grant Street is thinly built, with a few dwellings, sheds and a dairy near the southern end, and large empty areas. Block 210 between Grant and Liberty Streets has a regular row of small detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, and the heavy line at the east edge cuts off the old canal bed. Block 16 lies north of Gold Street and is blank apart from water pipes. Six-inch and four-inch high-service water pipes run in the streets, and fire alarm boxes and dwelling hydrants are marked. A large compass rose with a north arrow sits at the left. The drawing is entirely residential, with no industry, and no churches or schools. The heavy line at the right is the boundary with the Wharton strip, which is drawn at a different rotation. The scale bar at the foot reads 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Gold is Thompson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Liberty (German) is Liberty Street; Grant is Grant Street; Prospect is Prospect Street.

Georeferenced on two junctions (Grant and Liberty with Gold, 241 ft apart) at the configured scale; the Prospect and Gold junction was left out because its modern position is about 3 m from the drawn one.

50 ft. Two parts split by a vertical heavy line: 1 Prospect, Gold (Thompson Av.), Grant, Liberty (German); 2 Wharton strip (Pine (Mineola), N. Main, Furness Av. = Kossuth Av., Wharton Iron Foundry), north to the right.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is a narrow strip of the town of Wharton, drawn to the right of the heavy vertical line that divides it from Dover. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page, so the street lettering runs vertically. Pine, labelled Pine (Mineola), runs up the page as a 40 foot street between blocks 461 and 462, with house numbers on both sides; on the east side a row of eight small dwellings lettered B to J stands under block 462, and a single dwelling sits on the west side. Between Pine Street and the heavy line the old Morris Canal bed is lettered as filled in, and block 461 has a dwelling and a dividing line cutting across the canal bed. At the foot of the strip the Wharton Iron Foundry stands on the canal side with its stock house, cupola, earth floor, storage and shed, and its notes on watchman, power and lights. Below it the J. H. Jackson Lumber Co. coal yard has a coal shed with the note that its side is level with the ground, a cement storage building open under, and a switch tower. Railroad tracks fan out across the bottom, and North Main Street crosses diagonally with its 8 inch water pipe, joined by Furness Avenue running down to the lower left. Block 30 is lettered at the foot. The word Wharton is underlined beside the dwellings. The drawing shows only the edge of the Wharton settlement.
notes: North Main is North Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
Furness Av. is taken to be Kossuth Avenue (the old Furnace Street) on the spacing of Pine Street from North Main Street; low confidence.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Kossuth Avenue and North Main Street) at the configured scale with north to the right; low confidence.
The old canal bed is lettered as filled in.

50 ft. Two parts split by a vertical heavy line: 1 Prospect, Gold (Thompson Av.), Grant, Liberty (German); 2 Wharton strip (Pine (Mineola), N. Main, Furness Av. = Kossuth Av., Wharton Iron Foundry), north to the right.

sheet-12-1.description: The main part of sheet 12, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, covers a residential district on the south side of Dover between William Street and Liberty Street, from Gold Street on the west to Academy Street on the east. The page is turned so that William, Madison and Liberty streets run across it and Gold, Spruce, Pine and Academy streets run up and down it. Blocks 212, 213, 213 A, 365 and 211 are laid out in regular lots of frame dwellings, many with small auto sheds; much of blocks 213 A and 365 is still vacant lots. North of William Street, block 363 holds a row of small houses and, on Spruce Street, the Swiss Knitting Company plant, a knitting mill with engine and boiler rooms, lighted and powered by electricity. In the upper left corner a triangle of land toward Prospect Street is lettered Orchard St. Cemetery, with a few dwellings along its edges. The upper right corner is taken up by a separate boxed inset of the South Side Public School block (part 2), which lies elsewhere on Academy Street. Water pipes of 6 inches run in every street and hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: Gold is today's Thompson Avenue (confirmed by its spacing from Spruce and Pine streets).
Liberty is lettered with its older name (German) in brackets.

50 ft, north to the upper left. Part 1: William to Liberty (German), Gold (now Thompson Av.) to Academy; Swiss Knitting Co.; Orchard St. Cemetery. Part 2 (boxed inset, upper right): South Side Public School block 372 on Academy St., drawn on sheet 23 ground.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: South Side Public School, block 372 on Academy St. (no street junction; sheet 23 draws block 372 without the school and no shared corner could be matched; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-23 (block 372 corners) once a shared feature is identified).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 shows the area of Dover between the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad on the north and the Orchard Street Cemetery on the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. In the upper part the railroad curves across the sheet beside West Dickerson Street, with a freight depot of the railroad at the top right, lots of block 2 and a plant with a pink and yellow roof at the left, and the railroad tracks widening into yards at the top right. Bank Street runs east to west across the middle between blocks 29 and 30, and Chestnut Street runs below block 30. Orchard Street runs down the right side beside a row of numbered frame dwellings, with a larger building at the water edge, and Ford's Pond lies at the extreme right. Gold Street runs south from Chestnut Street between block 30 and the lots of block 12, and Prospect Street is the long street at the left with houses numbered along it. Elliott Street and Spring Street cross it from the left margin as dashed pipe lines. Most of the lower part of the sheet is the Orchard Street Cemetery, left blank with only a storage shed. The dwellings are mostly two storey frame buildings with porches; two buildings are brick or concrete. Ten inch water pipes run in Chestnut Street and along Prospect Street. A fire alarm box stands at the Chestnut and Orchard corner, and cuts A to B and C to D mark section lines.
notes: Gold is Thompson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Bank is Legion Place.
West Dickerson is along the railroad; Elliott Street and Spring Street are only the dashed pipes entering at the left edge.
Fitted scale is about 3 percent above the usual 50 ft constant.
50 ft. Prospect, Gold (Thompson Av.), Chestnut, Bank (Legion Place), Orchard; D.L.&W. R.R., Orchard Street Cemetery, Ford's Pond. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the south-eastern edge of the railroad district of Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs diagonally from the top to the bottom left with its yard tracks widening toward the bottom, and the streets beside it are South Dickerson on the east side and East Dickerson on the west side. Along South Dickerson stand a large pink factory building at the top, Swift and Company's Dover branch of dressed meats with its cooler and wagon sheds, Wolf's cleaning and dyeing works and a large garage for 50 cars with steam heat and electric lights. South Morris Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the rail corridor to Mountain Avenue at the lower right and is lined with numbered frame dwellings on its south side. Monmouth Avenue, marked not graded, runs north-east from South Morris Street between blocks 3 and 4, with frame dwellings on its south-western side. Mountain Avenue runs down the right margin, with Park Place and Hillcrest Avenue entering from the east as pipe lines. A signal machine shop of the railroad stands in the lower middle beside the stream and dam of Fords Pond. Large lots such as block 25 and A 1/3 are mostly unbuilt. The sheet edges South Bergen, South Essex and South Sussex Streets cross the top and left margins as dashed pipes.
notes: Hillcrest Av. and Park Pl. enter only as dashed pipes at the right edge.
Three of the five control points on Mountain Avenue are hand-picked; the fitted scale is about 4 percent above the usual 50 ft constant.
50 ft. Railroad, South and East Dickerson, South Morris, Monmouth Av., Mountain Av. One part; Mountain Av. junctions hand-picked.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the north-western residential and industrial part of Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top, slightly turned. West Blackwell Street runs across the upper half from the left edge to a viaduct and iron bridge over the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad at the right, with numbered frame dwellings along its south side. The railroad crosses the top of the sheet on an iron bridge over the Rockaway River, and Dover Pond and the Rockaway River fill the upper left. Between the viaduct and Dewey Street at the top right is an industrial group, including pink brick buildings of the auto printing tile and cement floor works, a baled hay warehouse, a furniture store and a garage with concrete floor and wooden roof, with Dewey Street running north from West Blackwell. Elliott Street crosses the middle of the sheet and bends toward Prospect Street at the right, where the F. O. E. Hall stands; Spring Street runs below it. Randolph runs north to south through the middle, and Elizabeth lies at the left margin beside blocks 205, 206, 207 and 21. The Gillen-Young Co. morgue stands at the left of block 205. Blocks 31 and 32 lie between West Blackwell and Elliott and between Elliott and Spring. Block C 1/4 at the bottom is largely open. Prospect Street runs diagonally down the right side with Chestnut Street entering from the east. The bottom edge carries a section line marked A to B.
notes: Elliott is Elliott Street; Randolph is Randolph Avenue; West Blackwell is West Blackwell Street.
Iron bridge and viaduct carry the railroad and West Blackwell Street at the right.
50 ft. West Blackwell, Elliott, Randolph, Spring, Prospect; Rockaway River, Dover Pond. One part.

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 shows the western residential district of Dover along Prospect Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The part lies left of the heavy diagonal line, which is the boundary with the Wharton strip. Prospect Street and Gold, two parallel diagonal streets, run from the lower left to the upper right across the middle of the part, lined with numbered frame dwellings on both sides, including a long row of attached houses near the top. Randolph Avenue runs down the top left between blocks 207 and C 1/4, and Elizabeth runs down the left margin. Lawrence Street crosses the left side from the left edge toward Prospect Street, and the lots above and below it are numbered blocks 207 and 208. At the lower left a pink tile building stands beside a small stone building, and a wide space of unsubdivided land lies below. Madison, Liberty and Grant Streets run south-east from Gold Street toward the heavy line, and William Street enters from the east near the top as a dashed pipe with a fire alarm box. Block 12 lies between Gold Street and the heavy line, and block 11 lies at the bottom beside the heavy line. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes run in the streets. A compass rose with the north arrow is at the top. The top edge carries section lines A to B and C.
notes: Gold is Thompson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Randolph Av. is Randolph Avenue; Madison St., Liberty St. and Grant St. are Madison Street, Liberty Street and Grant Street.
Liberty and Grant junctions with Gold are hand-picked; the Gold street centre was measured between its drawn edges, not on the pipe.
50 ft. Two parts split by a diagonal heavy line: 1 Prospect, Gold (Thompson Av.), Lawrence, Randolph Av.; 2 strip along W. Blackwell and Park Heights Av. at Hurd Park.

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is a strip of Wharton drawn to the right of the heavy diagonal line, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. West Blackwell Street runs diagonally across it from the lower left to the upper right, 60 feet wide with a lettered width of 52 and 60 feet, and carries a row of numbered frame dwellings on its eastern side, numbered from 190 to 230 and beyond. The old Morris Canal bed is lettered as filled in between West Blackwell and the heavy line, and block 12 and block 459 are lettered on either side. Park Heights Avenue, 40 feet wide, runs south from West Blackwell near the bottom with houses numbered 232, 234 and 236, and a 10 inch water pipe to Richard's Reservoir is marked beside it. Eight inch water pipes from the pumping station cross the open land, and a small brown brick building marked fire proof, concrete floor and reinforced concrete stands at the right near house 230. Hurd Park, block 361, is the wedge of open ground at the foot between the heavy line and Park Heights Avenue. A separate north arrow at the right points to the upper left. The heavy line itself is the boundary of the Dover sheet at the left. The part is thinly built and mostly open ground.
notes: W. Blackwell is West Blackwell Street; Park Heights Av. is Park Heights Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one hand-picked junction at the configured scale with north to the upper left; low confidence.
The old canal bed is lettered as filled in.
50 ft. Two parts split by a diagonal heavy line: 1 Prospect, Gold (Thompson Av.), Lawrence, Randolph Av.; 2 strip along W. Blackwell and Park Heights Av. at Hurd Park.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the northeast edge of Dover along the Rockaway River, between the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western yard at the left and the old Morris Canal bed at the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the street grid runs diagonally across the page. In the upper left North Salem and South Salem Streets cross the river on an iron bridge; South Salem carries lumber yards (the Standard Lumber Company Inc. with its lumber sheds, an office and store) and Harding Street is lettered as not opened. East Blackwell Street runs down the left side of the sheet past an auto service station, an iron foundry with pattern and moulding shops, a plumbing supplies warehouse, a garage and a junk yard, with frame dwellings on both sides. Richards Avenue runs south from North Salem Street with dwellings on its east side and joins Perry, Reeve, Palm, Sammisa Avenue and Lee Avenue. Sammisa Avenue is lined with dwellings on its north side. At the lower left stands the New Jersey Gas and Electric Company gas plant with two gas holders and a coal gas installation, set astride the City of Dover and Randolph Township line, and a curved railroad spur. The old Morris Canal bed, filled in and used as State Highway, curves down the right side. In the upper right Ekstrom Street meets East Mc Farlan Street. Large parts of the sheet between the streets are blank or numbered blocks without buildings.
notes: Hooey is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; Reeve is Reeves Street today, Sammisa Avenue is Sammis Avenue, Carrol is Carrol Street.
The old Morris Canal bed filled in and used as State Highway is East McFarlan Street today.
Harding is lettered 'not opened' on the sheet.
The modern Carrol Street / East Blackwell Street node lies about 20 m north of the drawn junction and was left out of the fit.
100 ft. East Blackwell and N./S. Salem east of downtown, Rockaway River, Harding, Richards Av., Carrol; Iron foundry, lumber yard. One part.

sheet-18-1.description: The lower part of sheet 18, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top, covers a residential district in the east of Dover between East McFarlan Street on the north and Richards Avenue on the south, from Union Street on the west to Lynn Street on the east. A heavy line separates it from the two industrial drawings above it. Mase Avenue and Myrtle Avenue run east from Mercer Street through regular blocks of frame dwellings, and Belmont Avenue runs diagonally south-east from the end of East McFarlan Street toward Lynn Street. Between Union and Mercer streets stands the Dover High School, a large brick building heated by steam and lighted by electricity. The bed of the old Morris Canal is marked as filled in along the south side of East McFarlan Street. A small brook runs south through block 203 B between Nelson Street and Lynn Street, beside the F. Ciardi and Company bottling plant and a general contractor's storage building. Brook Street is drawn as the southern continuation of Nelson Street toward Richards Avenue. Short stubs of Locust Avenue, Maple Street, Searing Street, Berry Street and Wayne Street are drawn where they meet McFarlan Street and Belmont Avenue. Water pipes and hydrants are shown in the streets. The blocks are numbered 135, 135 B, 203, 203 A and 203 B.
notes: Brook (between Myrtle Avenue and Richards Avenue) lies on the line of today's Nelson Street, which runs straight from Belmont Avenue to Richards Avenue; on the sheet Nelson and Brook are offset by about 40 ft at Myrtle Avenue.
The old Morris Canal bed along East McFarlan Street is marked as filled in.

100 ft, three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (lower): E. McFarlan to Richards Av., Union to Lynn; Dover High School. Part 2 (upper left, north to the upper right): D.L.&W. R.R. frog and switch shop, Rockaway River, E. Blackwell St. at Carrol St., Morris County Traction Co. car barns, Rockaway Township. Part 3 (upper right): Richardson & Boynton Co. stove works beside the railroads near W. Clinton St. (next to sheet 21), no street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Richardson & Boynton Co. stove works and city water works pumping station (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-21 or sheet-25 (rail lines, buildings drawn on both)).

sheet-18-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 18 is a separate drawing at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, of the railroad and river corridor east of Dover in Rockaway Township. The Rockaway River runs down the middle of the part, crossed by a foot bridge, with East Blackwell Street along its east bank and Carrol Street leaving Blackwell toward the east. West of the river a broad band of Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad tracks runs the length of the part, and beyond them stands the D. L. and W. R. R. frog and switch shop, a large erecting shop with machine, smith and switch shops, a round house, a storage building three hundred feet long and a concrete post manufactory. The Lackawanna Coal Company coal storage plant and its coal piles occupy the lower left. East of the river, on East Blackwell Street, are the car barns and repair shop of the Morris County Traction Company, a garage for eighteen cars at the corner of Carrol Street and a few dwellings. The area east of the river is lettered Rockaway Township. Hydrants with two hundred feet of hose are marked at the railroad shops.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Carrol Street / East Blackwell Street) with scale and rotation fixed; low confidence.
The printed north arrow points about 52 degrees clockwise from the top of the page; the modern line of East Blackwell Street and Carrol Street gives about 62 degrees, which was used.

100 ft, three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (lower): E. McFarlan to Richards Av., Union to Lynn; Dover High School. Part 2 (upper left, north to the upper right): D.L.&W. R.R. frog and switch shop, Rockaway River, E. Blackwell St. at Carrol St., Morris County Traction Co. car barns, Rockaway Township. Part 3 (upper right): Richardson & Boynton Co. stove works beside the railroads near W. Clinton St. (next to sheet 21), no street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Richardson & Boynton Co. stove works and city water works pumping station (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-21 or sheet-25 (rail lines, buildings drawn on both)).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the eastern part of Dover between Searing Street at the left and Stephen Street at the right, from Elm Street across the top to Perry Street and Richards Avenue at the lower left, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees. The upper left is a regular block pattern of frame dwellings along King, Berry and Clark Streets between Elm and East Mc Farlan Street, with a hall and a cafeteria near Searing Street and several private garages. East of Clark Street, Jackson Avenue runs north from East Mc Farlan Street, with larger undivided blocks (9A, 10A, 11A) to the north and small dwellings along Christopher, Cooper and Conger Streets. East Mc Farlan Street then runs south-south-east across the lower right with scattered buildings and a private road to the old slaughter house. In the lower left the Belmont Avenue district holds blocks of dwellings along Belmont Avenue, Wayne Street, Depew Avenue, Lynn Street and Trenton Street, including the Belmont Avenue Public School No. 3 with its steam heating. The old Morris Canal bed and its tow path, filled in and used as State Highway, run diagonally between Depew Avenue and the open block 449. Water pipes are lettered in most streets and street widths of 40 to 50 feet are given.
notes: The old Morris Canal bed filled in and used as State Highway, with the old tow path, is drawn through the lower middle of the sheet.
Belmont Avenue Public School No. 3 stands at Belmont Avenue and Depew Avenue.
The modern node where Belmont Avenue, East McFarlan Street and Searing Street meet was left out of the fit (modern East McFarlan Street is wider than drawn).
100 ft. East Dover: Searing, King, Berry, Clark, Jackson Av., Elm, Belmont Av., Depew Av., Trenton, Perry. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the dense residential and industrial blocks of Dover between Mount Hope Avenue at the left and Elm Street at the right, from Sampson Avenue near the top to Segur Street, McDavit Place and Locust Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees. A dash-dot line across the upper part marks the boundary between Rockaway Township and the City of Dover. North of it the blocks (101, 444, 445, 446, 447) are thinly built; south of it the blocks between Guy, Lincoln Avenue, Henry (Beech) and Oak Streets and the cross streets Clark, Berry, King, Searing and Maple Avenue are filled with frame dwellings. A printing company stands on Berry Street. The right centre is taken by the Onyx Hosiery Inc. silk stocking mills, a large brick and fireproof complex with a bridge between buildings and a fire risk note. At the bottom the New Jersey Power and Light Company garage, office and warehouse with a storage yard stands where Locust Avenue meets East McFarlan Street, beside the old Morris Canal bed. Locust Hill Cemetery adjoins at the lower left. Mount Hope Avenue curves down the left margin with scattered houses beyond it, and several parallel lines at the left are not streets.
notes: Henry is printed 'Henry (Beech)'; the street is Beech Street today.
Cooper is not matched to a modern street and was not used in the fit.
The old canal bed filled in follows East McFarlan Street at the lower right.
100 ft. North-east Dover: Sampson Av., Cooper, Stephen, Jackson Av., Henry (Beech), Lincoln Av., Mount Hope Av. One part.

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 21 is the main map of the north-western edge of Dover and the neighbouring village of Bowlbyville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top, slightly turned. It lies to the left of and below the heavy line that cuts off the Ann Street strip. Union Turnpike runs diagonally from the top to the lower middle, becoming West Clinton Street, and a dash-dot line marks the boundary between the village of Bowlbyville and the city of Dover across the upper left. Bowlbyville has Power Plant Road, Bowlby Avenue, Garrison Avenue, Berkshire Avenue and Jefferson Avenue running south to Leonard Street, with the Bowlbyville public school, block 424 and a few frame dwellings along the turnpike. In the Dover section North, Lemar, Center, Hillside, Davis, James and Baker Streets form a grid of frame dwellings between the turnpike and Baker Street, with block 438 and 439 near the middle. The Ulster Iron Works puddle department, with its blast furnaces, tank and sidings, stands on the left beside the railroad, and the hollow stay bolt department of the same works lies farther down beside West Clinton Street. At the bottom Goodale Avenue and Central Avenue cross to Pequannock Street, with dense dwellings in blocks 129 and 129A. Block 20A to the right is largely open. The scale bar reads 100 feet to an inch.
notes: West Clinton is West Clinton Street; Union Turnpike is West Union Turnpike in OpenStreetMap; Av. entries are Avenue streets.
The 'Av.' lettered beside Center may belong to a street labelled Center Av.; medium confidence.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Bowlbyville, Union Turnpike, W. Clinton, Davis, James, Baker, Lemar, Ulster Iron Works; 2 strip of Ann and Elizabeth Sts., Elliott to Lawrence, Dover General Hospital.

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21 is the Ann Street strip at the upper right of the page, bounded on the left and below by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows a residential district of Dover between Elliott Street at the top and Lawrence Street at the bottom. Ann runs down the left side of the strip and Elizabeth down the right, with block 22A of small frame dwellings between Elliott and Spring Streets at the top left, block 362 between Spring and Lawrence Streets, and block 23A and block 19A to the left of Ann Street. The Dover General Hospital stands at the left of the strip near the heavy line, drawn as a large frame building. Small groups of dwellings line Lawrence Street at the bottom and Ann and Elizabeth Streets, with block 24A below Lawrence. Elliott Street is lettered twice, once west of Elizabeth and once as Elliott St. east of it, where the street jogs south. Ten inch water pipes run in Elliott and Lawrence Streets, and a four inch pipe in Ann and Elizabeth Streets. A fire alarm box stands at Ann and Lawrence. The sheet number 21 and the Dover oval seal fall in the blank margin at the top. Blocks 15 and 16 are lettered on the right beyond the strip, showing where the neighbouring sheets continue. A north arrow at the right points to the upper left.
notes: Elliott west of Elizabeth is West Elliot Street and Elliott St. east of it is Elliott Street in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted scale about 4 percent above the 100 ft constant; two junctions were measured at ink threshold 100.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Bowlbyville, Union Turnpike, W. Clinton, Davis, James, Baker, Lemar, Ulster Iron Works; 2 strip of Ann and Elizabeth Sts., Elliott to Lawrence, Dover General Hospital.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows Bowlbyville, a gridded suburb on the northern edge of Dover along the Union Turnpike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. The turnpike runs down the left side at a slant, and the parallel avenues Garrison, Berkshire, Jefferson, Hillside and Highland run south from North Street, crossed by Turner, White, Grace, Sickles and Leonard Streets. Numbered blocks 378 to 419 fill the page; only the western blocks beside the turnpike and Garrison Avenue, and a few of the blocks around Berkshire and Hillside, have buildings, mostly small frame dwellings, with a garage on Leonard Street and an old concrete foundry lettered north of North Street. Most of the eastern blocks are drawn as empty lots with lot numbers only. Power Plant Road runs diagonally at the lower left, and Bowlby Avenue is the leftmost street of the grid. Street widths of 40 feet are lettered. No fire protection allowance is noted near the turnpike at the left. The bottom edge continues on sheet 21 and the boundary of the sheet at the right is blank for the next sheet.
notes: Sickles is Sickle Street in OpenStreetMap; Bowlby Avenue is Bowlby Street; Allen Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Leonard Street is a boundary street: only its north edge is drawn on this sheet, so its junctions were placed with a drawn width of 40 feet.
The sheet is drawn with 40 foot streets where today's rights of way are wider.
100 ft. Bowlbyville north of Leonard: Union Turnpike, Garrison, Berkshire, Jefferson, Turner, White, Grace, Sickles. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the southern edge of Dover where the city adjoins Randolph Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 40 degrees. Penn Avenue runs across the middle of the page, crossed by the numbered streets 2nd to 6th, and Crystal Street and Munson Avenue run roughly parallel to it below. In the upper left blocks 210, 211 and 365 hold dwellings along Liberty (German) Street and Madison Street, with South Street shown as not opened and a larger house and a coop in block 366; Kensington Avenue and William Street run through the open blocks to the east. The upper right is mostly empty blocks 372 and 373, bounded by the diagonal Academy Street and by 2nd Street, with Bryam Street branching off 2nd Street. Along Penn Avenue and Kearney Street dwellings are lined along blocks 367 to 371; blocks 25A, 26A and 143 along Crystal Street and Munson Avenue carry scattered dwellings, and Searing or Lange runs between them. A dash-dot line marks the City of Dover and Randolph Township boundary at the left, and Millbrook Avenue (Road) crosses the lower right corner. Water pipes are lettered in most streets.
notes: Block 372, bounded by Academy Street and 2nd Street at the upper right, is drawn here as empty.
Bryam Street is Byram Street today; Searing or Lange is Searing Lane.
Kensington Avenue and Madison Street join Penn Avenue within a few metres of 5th and 6th Streets in OpenStreetMap; those junctions were left out of the fit.
Liberty is lettered 'Liberty (German)'; South is lettered 'Not opened'.
100 ft. South Dover: Penn Av., Kensington Av., 2nd to 6th St., Munson Av., Millbrook Av., Kearney, Crystal. One part; control mostly along Penn Av. and 2nd St.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers central south Dover around South Morris Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 40 degrees. South Morris Street runs from Mountain Avenue at the top down to Munson Avenue and Millbrook Avenue (Road) at the bottom, with Park Avenue, Byram, New, Boonton, Livingston Avenue, Crystal Street and Munson Avenue crossing or branching from it. West of South Morris Street, 2nd and 1st Streets run south from Byram Street across Penn Avenue to Crystal Street, with blocks 137, 138, 141 and 142 of mostly frame dwellings; a brook and the open block 25 lie at the upper left. East of South Morris Street are blocks 139, 140, 140A to 140C and 214 to 216, again mostly dwellings, with Hillcrest Avenue (Grove), Park Place, Highland Avenue and Cross Street at the right and a Union Chapel with its steam heat and lights on the west side of South Morris Street at Crystal Street. The lower left is crossed by Millbrook Avenue (Road), a diagonal old road, with blocks 143, 143A and 143B, and Summer Street runs along the bottom. Several buildings are coloured as stores or institutions at the Crystal and Munson Street corners, and an old hose reel house with no hose is marked on South Morris Street.
notes: Crystal is West and East Chrystal Street in OpenStreetMap; Highland Avenue and Park Place are South Highland Avenue and Park Place; Byram is Byram Street, New is New Street.
Hillcrest Avenue is lettered 'Hillcrest Av. (Grove)'.
An old hose reel house, no hose, stands on South Morris Street near Munson Avenue.
100 ft. South-east Dover: Mountain Av., Hillcrest, Park Pl., Byram, Penn Av., 1st and 2nd St., Livingston Av., Summer. One part.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the western edge of Dover where it meets the Borough of Wharton. A dash-dot line running from the lower left to the upper right, lettered Borough of Wharton on one side and Town of Dover on the other, divides the sheet. West of the line, in Wharton, the map shows a large area of platted but almost empty blocks (numbers 314 to 320) laid out along Maryland, Wabash, Michigan, Elmira, Vassar and Lehigh streets and Hillsdale Drive, with a few dwellings, sheds and a pond at the upper left. East of the line, in Dover, the blocks between Baker Avenue and Princeton Avenue (300 to 305) are built up with frame dwellings, drawn at the east side of the sheet along the east-west streets Racine, Columbia, Rutgers, Yale and Harvard, with water pipes in the streets and fire alarm and hydrant symbols. Baker Avenue is also lettered Richardson Boulevard. Princeton Avenue runs along the old bed of the Morris Canal, lettered as filled in, between the street and the Rockaway River, which crosses the right side of the sheet with a bridge. At the bottom, West Blackwell Street runs along Hurd Public Park, and Highland Avenue and Walnut Street meet at the lower left. The large house marked Henry Baker stands on block 316. Sheet 26 adjoins on the left and sheet 32 below.
notes: Highland Avenue is today North Elk Avenue.
Baker Avenue is lettered with Richardson Boulevard in brackets; today it is Baker Avenue.
Elmira and Vassar are not in OpenStreetMap, and the platted streets of the Wharton side were not used as control.
The old Morris Canal bed east of Princeton Avenue is lettered as filled in.
The Borough of Wharton and Town of Dover boundary line crosses the sheet diagonally.
A fit through 14 junctions places the sheet at about 3.91 pixels per foot, as expected for 100 feet to an inch; the Wharton streets at the west have no control.
100 ft. Dover/Wharton line; Baker Av. to Princeton Av. (college-named streets), W. Blackwell and Hurd Public Park. One part.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the boundary between the Borough of Wharton and the Town of Dover along West Blackwell Street, west of the centre of Dover. The dash-dot line labelled Borough of Wharton and Town of Dover (city line) runs diagonally from the lower left to the right edge and divides the sheet. In Wharton, at the upper left, South Main Street runs north and south beside a large open parcel (block 342) holding the St. Mary's Roman Catholic church, St. Mary's school, a convent and a rectory, with Morris Brook flowing across the lower part of the parcel; Garden Street and the lots along it lie at the far left edge, and St. Mary's Street or Place crosses the top. East of South Main Street the blocks (343 to 353) are laid out along Cutler, Orange and Walnut streets, with Park, Ford, Ketchel, Downs, Lowe and Summit avenues running between them, and are built with frame dwellings on the western blocks and mostly empty lots toward the east. In Dover, below the line, West Blackwell Street (the road to Lake Hopatcong) runs east and west with dwellings on its south side (block 357), St. Mary's Hall, St. Mary's Avenue, Jardine Street (West Elm) and the Dover General Hospital, a large brick building on block 359. Hurd Street curves along a cemetery at the lower left and Drake Avenue, Elk Avenue and Highland Avenue run toward the bottom and right. Water mains of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in most streets and street widths of 40 to 60 feet are lettered.
notes: Highland Avenue and Elk Avenue are today North Elk Avenue.
Ketchel Avenue is today Kitchell Avenue.
South Main Street keeps its name in OpenStreetMap; Jardine (West Elm) is today Jardine Street.
West Blackwell Street is lettered as the road to Lake Hopatcong.
Fit at about 3.93 pixels per foot, as expected for 100 feet to an inch; the left strip along Garden Street and the cemetery at the lower left have no control points.
100 ft. Wharton/Dover line; S. Main, Ford, Ketchel (Kitchell), Downs, Summit, Cutler to Walnut, Hurd St., cemetery. One part.

sheet-27-1.description: Sheet 27, part 1, is the main map of the sheet and shows the central part of the Borough of Wharton along South Main Street. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a printed legend 'Wharton, entire sheet' beside the Dover oval, and the inset at the upper left (part 2) is cut out of it by a heavy line. South Main Street runs from the top right, past Clarence and Sterling streets, down to Hance Street, then bends south to Cutler Street at the lower right. Along it the frame dwellings stand close together, with lot numbers and house numbers marked. West of South Main Street, between Clarence and Sterling streets, block 330 and the large open Public Park take most of the upper middle of the sheet, with Robert Street shown as not opened. East of South Main Street the narrow blocks 333, 338 and 339 are bounded by Theodore Street, Division Street and Baltimore Street, all marked not opened, and by Union Street and Theodore Street at the top. The lower half is a mostly open tract (blocks 340, 340A and 343) crossed by Hance Street, also lettered Alice Lane, Maple Terrace and Birmingham Lane, where dwellings, an auto repair shop and a store stand. At the bottom the curved St. Marys Street or Place runs from the lower left to South Main Street, with the long narrow lots of block 341A on its north side, and Carter Avenue and Garden Street at the bottom left. Water pipes are drawn in most of the streets and street widths of 40 to 50 feet are lettered.
notes: Hance (Alice Lane) is lettered with the old name in brackets; Hance Street is the modern name.
Robert, Theodore, Division and Baltimore streets are lettered 'not opened' on the sheet.
The fit comes out at about 4.05 pixels per foot, about 3 percent above the usual 100 foot scale constant for this atlas.
Junctions on St. Marys Street and on Division and Sterling streets were left out of the fit because they sat 4 to 5 metres off.

100 ft. Wharton (entire sheet): S. Main, Sterling, Baltimore, Hance, Division, Theodore, St. Marys St. or Pl. Part 1 main; part 2 inset at upper left (Carter Av. and Garden at W. Blackwell), placed by a point carried from sheet 26. Part 1 fits 3.6 percent above the scan constant.

sheet-27-2.description: Sheet 27, part 2, is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, separated from the main map by a heavy line that runs down the right side and then turns to the lower left. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing straight up, and shows Carter Avenue and Garden Street in the Borough of Wharton, running north and south between lot lines of blocks 341 and 341A. The map is lettered with house numbers and lot depths of about 50 feet. Frame dwellings and small outbuildings line the lots on both avenues, and a junk dealer's building marked not in use stands midway down the block between the two. Morris Brook runs across the middle of the inset from the left, passes under Garden Street on a small bridge and ends at the heavy line, where it continues on sheet 26. A 6 inch water main is drawn in Garden Street, ending near the brook. At the foot of the inset West Blackwell Street, also lettered as the road to Lake Hopatcong, runs east and west, and a one-story fireproof power substation of the Morris County Traction Company stands at its north edge, with block 30A below. The inset shows the ground directly west of the strip along Garden Street at the left edge of sheet 26.
notes: The inset shows Garden Street drawn straight up the page; on sheet 26 the same street is tilted about 15 degrees.
Placed from one point carried from sheet 26 (the corner of Garden Street and West Blackwell Street) with the scale and rotation of sheet 26, so its position and rotation are approximate.

100 ft. Wharton (entire sheet): S. Main, Sterling, Baltimore, Hance, Division, Theodore, St. Marys St. or Pl. Part 1 main; part 2 inset at upper left (Carter Av. and Garden at W. Blackwell), placed by a point carried from sheet 26. Part 1 fits 3.6 percent above the scan constant.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the middle of the Borough of Wharton just south of its centre, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the north arrow pointing to the upper right, so the streets run on a diagonal across the page. South Main Street enters at the top left near Thomas Street, with a garage and several frame dwellings along its east side, and runs south and south-west, curving past Oak Lane and Union Street. Union Street runs south-west from Baker Avenue, lettered also as Frederick, to join South Main Street, and Theodore and Clarence streets cross at the lower left. East of Baker Avenue the long blocks 150A, 150B and 151 stretch to East Central Avenue, lettered Poppenhusen East, with a row of closely built frame dwellings along Baker Avenue and a few along East Central. The Knights of Pythias hall, a three-storey frame building with lodge rooms, stands on Baker Avenue, and a cement block manufactory with an electric motor stands on block 150B. Church Street and the proposed 3rd Street come in from the right edge, and Thomas Street runs across the top. Water mains of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets, and street widths of 40 to 60 feet are lettered. The Wharton boundary lettering appears at the right, with sheets 29, 30 and 27 named at the edges.
notes: Baker Avenue is lettered 'Baker Av. (Frederick)' and East Central Avenue 'E. Central Av. (Poppenhusen E.)'; the bracketed names are the older names.
3rd Street is lettered proposed.
Fit at about 7.9 pixels per foot, as expected for 50 feet to an inch, with a rotation of about 46 degrees.
50 ft. Wharton: S. Main, Oak Lane, Union, Baker Av. (Frederick), E. Central Av. (Poppenhusen E.), Thomas. One part.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 shows the centre of the Borough of Wharton and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. A heavy line lettered Wharton runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right across the sheet; beside it at the lower left the notation 'no exposure' marks the wall of the buildings on the line, and the town streets continue on both sides at the same angle. In the upper left the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs in a bundle of tracks toward the upper right, with the railroad crossing West Central Avenue (also lettered Poppenhusen West), Gallegher Road (also Railroad Avenue) and Irondale Road on the left. Along West Central Avenue are frame dwellings on blocks 145A and 145B. The middle of the sheet holds the Wharton High School, a large pink brick building with an auditorium, gymnasium and balcony, and the Wharton Public School a little to the east. At the right edge West Central Avenue, East Central Avenue and North Main Street meet at the Town Hall, which houses the fire department and police station, near a post office, a bake house with a flour store and a row of stores. South Main Street leads down to Thomas Street at the bottom, with Robert Street and Mill Street leaving it on the left. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 inches are drawn, including a 12 inch main on Gallegher Road from the reservoir and a 10 inch main running to the pumping station.
notes: The heavy line lettered Wharton with 'no exposure' is a wall line and not a break in the street grid, so the sheet is georeferenced as one part.
Baker Avenue is lettered at the bottom edge; East Central Avenue and West Central Avenue carry the older name Poppenhusen in brackets.
Gallegher Road is lettered 'Gallegher Rd. (Railroad Av.)'.
Fit at about 8.0 pixels per foot with a rotation of about 46 degrees; the upper half of the sheet has only one hand-picked control point.

50 ft. Wharton centre: W. Central Av., S. Main, Robert, Mill, Irondale Rd., Gallegher Rd.; Wharton High School and Public School. The heavy line lettered Wharton is a boundary, not a part divider. One part; control in the lower part.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 shows the centre of Wharton, the borough west of Dover, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right of the page. West Central Avenue and East Central Avenue, each lettered with its former name Poppenhusen, run down the left edge and join sheet 29 and sheet 28. North Main crosses the upper left and runs toward the upper right past the Central Hotel, a tin shop, an auto repairing shop in a pink-coloured building and a row of stores. Hurd Lane, also lettered Towbridge Lane, runs up the page beside block 146. Washington runs across the middle of the sheet to Furnace Avenue, and Fern Avenue, which also carries the lettering Canal, runs down the page along the line of the old Morris Canal. South of Washington the blocks are mostly frame dwellings between 2nd Street and Church, with the Wharton Ho. on the corner of East Central Avenue, St. John's M.E. Church and its old church on Church Street and Mt. Pleasant, and H. G. De Mott coal and trucking with a wagon shed beside Fern Avenue. At the top right the J. H. Jackson Lumber Company yard, with a long lumber shed, a carpenter shop, storage of building materials and open lumber piles, lies beside the railroad tracks that run past the name Wharton. The old canal bed is marked as filled in east of Fern Avenue, and Orchard and Mt. Hope St. open off Furnace Avenue on the right side of the sheet. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn in most streets, and street widths of 30 to 50 feet are lettered. The compass rose and scale bar fill the lower right corner, and neighbouring sheets are numbered 28, 29 and 32 at the margins.
notes: Central Avenue is lettered with the former names Poppenhusen West and Poppenhusen East; today West Central Avenue and East Central Avenue.
Hurd Lane is lettered with the second name Towbridge Lane; the modern name is Trowbridge Lane.
Fern Avenue is lettered with the former name Canal; it follows the bed of the Morris Canal.
Furnace Avenue is today Kossuth Avenue; Washington is today Washington Street; North Main is today North Main Street.
Mount Pleasant is today Mount Pleasant Avenue; Church is today Church Street; Grove is today Grove Street.
Thomas Street at the left edge is today East Thomas Street and West Thomas Street.
The old canal bed east of Fern Avenue is marked as filled in.
50 ft. Wharton centre: W. and E. Central Av. (Poppenhusen), N. Main, Washington, Fern Av. (Canal), Furnace Av. (Kossuth), 2nd, Church, Mt. Pleasant, Grove. One part.

sheet-31-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 31, the northern edge of the Wharton centre. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north turned about 17 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. East Dewey Avenue runs across the upper middle and right of the sheet beside blocks 324 and 325, with small frame dwellings set on narrow lots on both sides. To the west it becomes West Dewey Avenue, which carries the second name Broadway and runs down to the left edge past a tile works, a general store and the Luxemburg Presbyterian Church. High and Luxemburg Avenue run diagonally across the upper left through blocks 321, 321A and 322. North Main enters from the top at the match line with sheet 33, crosses East Dewey Avenue and runs south-east, with Ross leaving it toward the east. South of Ross the road runs along the Rockaway River past the large Onyx Hosiery Inc. plant, makers of silk stockings, with its manufacturing, packing and office buildings coloured pink and brown, and crosses the river on an iron bridge near the foot of the sheet. A coal and building supply yard stands beside Washington Forge Pond on the left. The Replogle Steel Company's Orchard Mine, marked not in operation 1926, with crusher house, head house, machine shop and engine room, fills the lower left corner below the boxed inset. That inset, drawn at a different rotation and showing the Onyx Hosiery works on the river, has its own north arrow and is not part of this mask. A Central Railroad of New Jersey line runs along the lower right edge. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn along the streets, and the street widths of 30 to 50 feet are lettered.
notes: West Dewey Avenue is lettered with the second name Broadway.
High is today High Street; North Main is today North Main Street; Ross is today Ross Street.
The drawn Luxemburg Avenue does not follow the modern Luxemburg Avenue in OpenStreetMap, which was left out of the fit.
Georeferenced from one point at East Dewey Avenue and North Main Street with the scale and north set by hand; the modern Ross Street junction lies about 12 m from where this placement puts it.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 Wharton, E. and W. Dewey Av. (Broadway), N. Main, Ross, Luxemburg Av., High; Onyx Hosiery works; anchored on one junction. 2 boxed inset at lower left, rotated: Onyx Hosiery Inc. plant on the Rockaway River, no street junction. Luxemburg Av. and High St. drawn off their modern lines.

sheet-32-2.description: The upper right part of sheet 32 is a separate drawing at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the right of the page, of the Hurd Park area on the western side of Dover. West Blackwell Street runs down the right-hand side of the part from Elk Avenue at the top past Hillsdale Drive and Baker Avenue to Princeton Avenue at the bottom, where a heavy line divides it from the amusement park inset below. Park Heights Avenue runs down the left-hand side. Between them lies Hurd Park, with its lake, a smaller pond and Granny's Brook winding through it. On the brook in the upper left stands the Singleton silk mill, formerly a group of buildings including an old dye house, an old machine shop and a vacant main building, all marked vacant except the engine and boiler rooms. A private road crosses the park toward Blackwell Street. Along Elk Avenue at the top are a few dwellings in block 361, and two small buildings on Park Heights Avenue include the Sievers violin studio. Block 459 to the west is left blank. A hydrant and fire alarm box stand at Baker Avenue.
notes: Placed from three junctions along West Blackwell Street (Elk hand-picked, Baker and Princeton detected), an exact three-point fit; low to medium confidence.
Highland Avenue (lettered T. H. Highland Av. at the top right) has no modern counterpart in the reference data.

100 ft, three parts. Part 1 (left, largest): Replogle Steel Co. ore yard, reservoir and engine house in Wharton, no street junction except Mt. Hope St. at the top edge. Part 2 (upper right, north to the right): Hurd Park, Singleton silk mill, W. Blackwell St. from Elk to Princeton Av. Part 3 (lower right): Colonial Gate Amusement Park, 1 1/2 miles SE of the Town Hall, no streets.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Replogle Steel Co. ore yard (Wharton) (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-30 (Mt. Hope St., rail lines) or parcel corners).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Colonial Gate Amusement Park (no street junction; location given only as 1 1/2 miles SE of the Town Hall).

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the open country north of the built-up part of Wharton along North Main, where the road runs north-east from the foot of the sheet to a fork near the top. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north tilted about 16 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. Most of the sheet is blank. Frame dwellings stand along North Main, and a block of narrow lots on Langdon, with the lane Robin Red Breast running between lots, lies west of the road in the middle of the sheet. At the top, North Main forks into Union Turnpike, which continues north-west toward sheet 34, a second Union Turnpike running south-east, and a short street lettered Ase St. (Arbitrary). Billie Lee, also marked Arbitrary, is a short 35 foot street laid out on paper off the west side of the south-east Union Turnpike. Burnt Meadow Brook crosses the upper right corner, with a road of 50 feet width beside it leading to the Mt. Pleasant Public School, heated by steam and without lights. At the lower left a mine with an engine room, hoist and other small buildings is marked Abandoned Mine, and a curved railroad siding sweeps across the lower middle and runs to the foot of the sheet. A match line A-B near the foot joins sheet 31, a dash-dot line, and the sheet numbers 34, 31, 36A, 37A, 38A and 39A mark the neighbouring sheets and the large blank blocks. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along North Main and Union Turnpike. The scale bar and library stamp are at the bottom.
notes: Ase Street is lettered Ase St. with the word Arbitrary below it, meaning a street name given to a proposed street; the first letter may be missing from the lettering and the name has not been matched to a modern street.
Billie Lee is also marked Arbitrary and is not in the modern street network.
North Main is today North Main Street; Langdon is today Langdon Avenue.
Union Turnpike north of the fork lies under or beside the modern NJ 15 highway; the junction at the fork is not in OpenStreetMap.
A road lettered only Road, 50 feet wide, leads to the Mt. Pleasant Public School at the upper right.
Placed from one point at North Main and Langdon with the scale and north set by hand, so low confidence.
100 ft. North Main north of Wharton, Langdon, Union Turnpike fork, Billie Lee (arbitrary), Burnt Meadow Brook; mostly blank. Anchored on one junction.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 shows the sparsely built country north of Wharton in Rockaway Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right of the page, about 50 degrees clockwise from the top. Union Turnpike, lettered Union Tnpk., runs up the page as a 66 foot road with frame dwellings and small outbuildings strung along its west side on long narrow lots. A dash-dot line across the middle marks the boundary between Rockaway Township and the Town of Wharton, and the name Wharton is lettered at the left. Near that boundary Wilmuth, marked Arbitrary, is a 40 foot cross street laid out on paper west of the turnpike. Government's Road, 35 and 50 feet wide, leaves the turnpike and runs north-east across Burnt Meadow Brook, with a note To Picatinny Arsenal, and Spicertown Road branches from it toward a small cluster of dwellings and lots, one of them lettered L. Kimble. The brook winds down the page from the top to a bridge on the Ase street at the foot, near a vacant factory beside the turnpike. At the bottom left North Main Street joins the turnpike at a fork, where the sheet overlaps the top of sheet 33; the match is shown by the sheet number 33 and the dash-dot match line. Dashed lines of 4 and 6 inch water pipe run beside the turnpike. Blocks 31A, 32A, 33A, 34A, 35A and 36A are numbered across the blank areas. The north arrow is at the upper left, and a library stamp, scale bar and copyright line are at the bottom right.
notes: Union Tnpk. is lettered without the full word; today the road follows the line of NJ 15 and West Union Turnpike or Union Turnpike in OpenStreetMap, and no junction on the sheet matches a modern junction.
Wilmuth is marked Arbitrary and is not in the modern street network.
Ase is lettered Ase on this sheet and Ase St. on sheet 33; it has not been matched to a modern street.
Government's Road leads to Picatinny Arsenal; it has not been matched with certainty to a modern road.
Placed only by a point carried from sheet 33 (the fork of North Main and Union Turnpike), with scale and north set by hand, so low confidence.
100 ft. Union Turnpike in Rockaway Township (now NJ 15), Wilmuth (arbitrary), Government Rd. to Picatinny Arsenal, Spicertown Rd. Placed by one pipe junction carried from sheet 33.
